title: Route/Model Cost Drivers – Dataset Schema (proposed aggregates + queries)
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-16 (Mei)

Purpose
- Define the aggregate datasets powering Console → Usage Insights:
  - Top cost drivers by route
  - Route detail → model breakdown
  - “What changed” (compare current window vs prior window)
  - Export reports (bounded CSV/JSON)

Non-goals (for this schema doc)
- Invoice-grade reconciliation (we’ll document known causes of drift).
- Custom customer-defined dimensions beyond route/model.


TAB: Overview (high-level)
Data flow (simplified)
1) Raw metering + telemetry events land in warehouse (token accounting, latency, errors).
2) Normalize/enforce route dimension (SDK header preferred; gateway-derived fallback).
3) Hourly aggregates (near-real-time, used for UI time ranges ≤ 7d and sparklines).
4) Daily aggregates (cheaper queries, used for longer ranges and week-over-week deltas).
5) Export materializes a bounded “report dataset” by re-querying aggregates (not raw) and freezing filters in an audit event.

Warehouse assumptions
- SQL dialect: Postgres-compatible (for examples) but tables should be implementable in ClickHouse/BigQuery-style partitioned storage.
- Aggregation freshness target: hourly tables T+10–20m typical; allow late arrivals within 48h via upserts/backfill.

Key identifiers
- org_id / project_id: tenant boundaries.
- environment: prod | staging | dev (from project config / request context).
- deployment_mode: hosted_api | dedicated | private (as we expose in Console filters).


TAB: Tables (proposed)

Table 1: usage_insights_route_model_hourly
Grain
- 1 row per (org_id, project_id, environment, region, deployment_mode, route_id, model_id, hour)

Partitioning / clustering
- Partition: hour_ts (by day) OR (dt = date(hour_ts)) depending on warehouse
- Cluster/sort keys: org_id, project_id, route_id, model_id

Retention
- 30 days default (matches near-real-time UI needs; confirm with Product)

Columns
| column | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| hour_ts | timestamptz | Y | Start of hour in UTC (e.g., 2026-02-16 14:00:00+00) |
| dt | date | Y | Derived partition key = date(hour_ts) |
| org_id | text | Y | Tenant org |
| project_id | text | Y | Tenant project |
| environment | text | Y | prod/staging/dev; default=prod |
| region | text | Y | e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1; “unknown” allowed |
| deployment_mode | text | Y | hosted_api/dedicated/private |
| route_id | text | Y | Canonical normalized route (see Route normalization below) |
| route_source | text | Y | sdk | gateway | none |
| route_is_overflow | boolean | Y | True if cardinality guardrail bucketed to overflow route |
| route_hash | text | Y | Stable hash of pre-normalized route for internal debugging (NOT exposed) |
| model_id | text | Y | Canonical model identifier (e.g., llama-3.1-70b-instruct) |
| model_variant | text | N | Optional serving variant label (e.g., “baseline”, “fallback-a10g”) |
| quant_profile | text | N | e.g., fp16, int8, awq-int4; may be null |
| request_count | bigint | Y | Count of requests observed in this hour |
| success_count | bigint | Y | Requests with non-error completion |
| error_count | bigint | Y | Request-level errors (HTTP 4xx/5xx mapped per API contract) |
| input_tokens | bigint | Y | Metered prompt tokens |
| output_tokens | bigint | Y | Metered completion tokens |
| cached_input_tokens | bigint | Y | Tokens served from cache (prefix/KV); may be 0 |
| billed_input_tokens | bigint | Y | Tokens that contribute to usage charges (post-cache) |
| billed_output_tokens | bigint | Y | Usually equals output_tokens; kept for symmetry/future |
| gpu_time_ms | bigint | N | Proxy if available; may be null in some deployments |
| cost_usd | numeric(18,6) | Y | Attributed usage cost for the row (see cost attribution notes) |
| unit_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | numeric(18,6) | N | Convenience field; derived at query time in many engines |
| latency_ms_sum | bigint | Y | Sum of latencies (ms) for avg latency |
| latency_ms_count | bigint | Y | Count for avg latency |
| latency_ms_p50 | integer | N | Approx/TDigest percentile; engine-specific |
| latency_ms_p95 | integer | N | Approx/TDigest percentile; engine-specific |
| created_at | timestamptz | Y | Insert time |
| updated_at | timestamptz | Y | Last upsert time |

Notes
- Percentiles: store p50/p95 as approximate aggregate output per hour. For engines that support mergeable sketches, consider storing sketch blobs instead; for this first version we store p50/p95 directly.


Table 2: usage_insights_route_model_daily
Grain
- 1 row per (org_id, project_id, environment, region, deployment_mode, route_id, model_id, day)

Partitioning / clustering
- Partition: day (date)
- Cluster: org_id, project_id, route_id

Retention
- 13 months proposed (to support typical FinOps/QBR workflows; align with Insights retention policy)

Columns
- Same as hourly, with day instead of hour_ts:

Table 3: usage_insights_route_daily (route summary table)
Why
- Speed up “Top routes” list without forcing GROUP BY over model_id for wide time ranges.

Grain
- 1 row per (org_id, project_id, environment, region, deployment_mode, route_id, day)

Derivation
- SUM metrics across models for the route/day.

Columns

Table 4 (optional for export stability): usage_insights_export_snapshot
Why
- Exports should be reproducible for a period even if aggregates receive late-arriving corrections.
- This table is written by the export job worker (bounded output only).

Grain
- 1 row per export_job_id per aggregate row included.

Retention
- 30 days (align with export download TTL + audit evidence needs)

Columns (minimal)
| column | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| export_job_id | text | Y | From export service |
| generated_at | timestamptz | Y |  |
| org_id | text | Y |  |
| project_id | text | Y |  |
| window_start | timestamptz | Y | Frozen filter |
| window_end | timestamptz | Y | Frozen filter |
| environment | text | Y | Frozen filter |
| region | text | Y | Frozen filter or “*” |
| deployment_mode | text | Y | Frozen filter or “*” |
| route_id | text | Y |  |
| model_id | text | N | Null for route-only exports |
| cost_usd | numeric(18,6) | Y |  |
| input_tokens | bigint | Y |  |
| output_tokens | bigint | Y |  |
| cached_input_tokens | bigint | Y |  |
| billed_input_tokens | bigint | Y |  |
| request_count | bigint | Y |  |
| error_count | bigint | Y |  |


TAB: Route normalization + cardinality controls
Canonical route rules (summary; see ADR for full details)
- Prefer SDK-provided route identifier (e.g., x-redwood-route), else gateway-derived (HTTP route template), else “unknown”.
- Length limit: 128 chars (truncate after normalization).
- Allowed charset: [a-zA-Z0-9:/._-] (others replaced with ‘_’).
- No dynamic identifiers: never include user_id, request_id, UUIDs, email, etc.

Cardinality guardrails (implementation notes)
- Per (org_id, project_id, environment) maintain a rolling set of top N routes/day (N default 2,000; TBD).
- Routes outside top N are bucketed into:
  - route_id = "/__overflow__" (route_is_overflow=true)
- When route is missing:
  - route_id = "/__unknown__" (route_source=none)
- Keep route_hash for internal debugging and for support escalations (do NOT expose in Console/export by default).


TAB: Cost attribution notes
- cost_usd is attributed per request and aggregated.
- For smart routing/model fallback:
  - The route dimension is the original request route.
  - model_id is the model that actually served tokens.
  - If a single request spans multiple model_ids (rare; e.g., mid-stream fallback), we split the request into multiple metering segments and aggregate accordingly.
- cached_input_tokens reduce billed_input_tokens; cost is computed on billed_* tokens where applicable.
- gpu_time_ms is best-effort and may be null depending on deployment mode/instrumentation.

Known reasons aggregates may not match invoice totals exactly (to be documented in Support FAQ)
- Different cutoffs/timezones for billing cycles vs UI time windows.
- Late arriving metering adjustments (we upsert aggregates within a window).
- Rounding in unit cost fields.
- Backfill changes after a schema/version rollout.


TAB: Example queries (powering console)

Query A: Top routes by cost (last 7 days, route summary)
-- Inputs: :org_id, :project_id, :env, :start_day, :end_day, :region (optional), :deployment_mode (optional)
SELECT
  route_id,
  SUM(cost_usd) AS cost_usd,
  SUM(request_count) AS request_count,
  SUM(error_count) AS error_count,
  CASE WHEN SUM(request_count) > 0
       THEN (SUM(error_count)::numeric / SUM(request_count)::numeric)
       ELSE 0 END AS error_rate,
  CASE WHEN SUM(latency_ms_count) > 0
       THEN (SUM(latency_ms_sum)::numeric / SUM(latency_ms_count)::numeric)
       ELSE NULL END AS avg_latency_ms
FROM usage_insights_route_daily
WHERE org_id = :org_id
  AND project_id = :project_id
  AND environment = :env
  AND day >= :start_day
  AND day < :end_day
  AND (:region IS NULL OR region = :region)
  AND (:deployment_mode IS NULL OR deployment_mode = :deployment_mode)
GROUP BY route_id
ORDER BY cost_usd DESC
LIMIT 100;


Query B: Route detail (model breakdown) for a time window
-- Use route_model_daily for longer windows; route_model_hourly for short windows.
SELECT
  model_id,
  SUM(cost_usd) AS cost_usd,
  SUM(input_tokens) AS input_tokens,
  SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
  SUM(cached_input_tokens) AS cached_input_tokens,
  SUM(request_count) AS request_count,
  SUM(error_count) AS error_count
FROM usage_insights_route_model_daily
WHERE org_id = :org_id
  AND project_id = :project_id
  AND environment = :env
  AND route_id = :route_id
  AND day >= :start_day
  AND day < :end_day
  AND (:region IS NULL OR region = :region)
  AND (:deployment_mode IS NULL OR deployment_mode = :deployment_mode)
GROUP BY model_id
ORDER BY cost_usd DESC
LIMIT 50;


Query C: “What changed” delta (current window vs prior window)
-- window length is determined by UI selection; prior window is immediately preceding.
WITH
current AS (
  SELECT route_id, SUM(cost_usd) AS cost_usd
  FROM usage_insights_route_daily
  WHERE org_id = :org_id AND project_id = :project_id AND environment = :env
    AND day >= :cur_start AND day < :cur_end
  GROUP BY route_id
),
prior AS (
  SELECT route_id, SUM(cost_usd) AS cost_usd
  FROM usage_insights_route_daily
  WHERE org_id = :org_id AND project_id = :project_id AND environment = :env
    AND day >= :prior_start AND day < :prior_end
  GROUP BY route_id
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(c.route_id, p.route_id) AS route_id,
  COALESCE(c.cost_usd, 0) AS current_cost_usd,
  COALESCE(p.cost_usd, 0) AS prior_cost_usd,
  (COALESCE(c.cost_usd, 0) - COALESCE(p.cost_usd, 0)) AS delta_cost_usd,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(p.cost_usd, 0) > 0
       THEN (COALESCE(c.cost_usd, 0) - COALESCE(p.cost_usd, 0)) / COALESCE(p.cost_usd, 0)
       ELSE NULL END AS delta_cost_pct
FROM current c
FULL OUTER JOIN prior p
  ON c.route_id = p.route_id
ORDER BY delta_cost_usd DESC
LIMIT 100;


Query D: Hourly sparkline for a single route (past 24h)
SELECT
  hour_ts,
  SUM(cost_usd) AS cost_usd
FROM usage_insights_route_model_hourly
WHERE org_id = :org_id
  AND project_id = :project_id
  AND environment = :env
  AND route_id = :route_id
  AND hour_ts >= :start_ts
  AND hour_ts < :end_ts
GROUP BY hour_ts
ORDER BY hour_ts ASC;


TAB: Open questions / TODO
- Confirm retention targets for daily tables (Product/Security): 13 months vs 6 months.
- Percentiles implementation: keep p50/p95 columns vs store sketch blobs for mergeability.
- Define model_id canonicalization across hosted/dedicated/private (especially for “compatible variants”).
- Export snapshot necessity: keep as optional until we observe late-arrival confusion in beta.
- Decide whether to persist unit_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd or always compute at query time.

Changelog
- 2026-02-16: Added route_daily summary table + export_snapshot option; clarified fallback attribution split.
- 2026-02-05: First pass hourly/daily schemas aligned to route normalization + cardinality flags.
